messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 SEV2 | Service: inference-api | symptom: elevated 5xx rate > 4% | affected: hosted/text-generation | ts=1748453210

alex: acked — I'm on it, pulling logs and checking recent deploys

maya: ack — looking at the autoscaler dashboards, CPU/GPU nodes look healthy

sre_lead: thanks. alex, prioritize customer-impact first. cs_jordan, any high-priority customer threads? we should flag externally if necessary

cs_jordan: we have one active ticket from DeltaHealth complaining about timeouts in the chat feature. CS put them on priority, waiting for root cause

alex: quick grep on prod logs shows repeated errors: "KVCacheMissError" and downstream timeout 504 from runtime-proxy

alex: dumping recent deploys... nothing pushed in the last 3 hours. rolling restarts? no

maya: adding tracers. latency spike aligns with a surge at 12:02 UTC — sudden small burst of long-context requests

ops-taylor: checked the routing table, a new model variant was temporarily added to the routing policy at 12:01 by experiments service

sre_lead: that might explain it — experiments created a heavier quantized model route, causing memory pressure and KV cache misses

alex: mitigation plan: 1) remove experiment route 2) flush KV cache on affected nodes 3) restart runtime-proxy on two nodes as canary

maya: executing step 1 now — disabling route id exp-293

incident-bot: route exp-293 disabled by maya at 1748453350

alex: flushing KV caches: running

alex: code snippet I ran:
```
# flush kv on targets
curl -X POST https://infra.internal/kvcache/flush -d '{"shard":"s-3"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

maya: canary restart of runtime-proxy on node gpu-17 started

ops-taylor: keeping watch on metrics, GPU memory usage down ~12% after cache flush

cs_jordan: DeltaHealth reports partial recovery, they see drop in errors but still occasional timeouts

alex: rolling restart complete for canary, error rate on canary node now ~0.3% (baseline 0.1)

sre_lead: good. continue gradual restart across pool with 30s drain windows

maya: continuing restarts, starting batch 2/5

alex: also found a small memory leak in the kernel selection path when the heavy model variant is used — opened PR to revert the model binary until we investigate deeper: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/412

product-emma: tagging for post-incident: need to decide on rollout guardrails for experiment routes and model size thresholds

ops-taylor: paging summary for on-call handoff: current status partial mitigation, error rate trending down from 4.7% -> 0.8%, still above SLA threshold

sre_lead: can we quantify customer impact? cs_jordan?

cs_jordan: affected ~6 customers; 2 had degraded UX (longer timeouts), 1 had billing-sensitive flow impacted (DeltaHealth). No data exfiltration

alex: putting notes in incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2025

maya: metrics now at 0.4% overall, latency P95 back to near baseline

incident-bot: escalation timer set — next on-call: rajan in 2h. Handoff required if not resolved before then.

alex: agree we should rotate if still in monitoring state. I'll start a structured handoff message 30m before shift change

sre_lead: action items (assign now):
- alex: follow up on PR revert + quick regression test (due: 2025-03-12T17:00Z)
- maya: run forensic on KV cache behavior and produce a short report (due: 2025-03-14T00:00Z)
- product-emma: propose experiment rollout guardrail (due: 2025-03-18T00:00Z)
- ops-taylor: update runbook to include \"disable experiment route\" steps and KV flush commands (due: 2025-03-13T12:00Z)

cs_jordan: I'll draft customer comms for DeltaHealth and the 5 other customers, will loop in legal if needed

product-emma: plan brown-bag for infra+product next week to cover experiment safety and rollout policies

alex: flagging technical note: temporary mitigation may mask deeper kernel bug; need follow-up eval on long contexts

ops-taylor: created follow-up checklist in the incident doc, linking to logs and dashboards

incident-bot: incident status changed to MONITORING at 1748454920

maya: starting to prepare postmortem meeting — propose Wed 2025-03-16 16:00 UTC (1h). Thoughts?

product-emma: works for me

sre_lead: works

cs_jordan: ok, I'll invite DeltaHealth contact to optional sync

ops-taylor: I'll prepare the incident timeline and runbook diffs

alex: handoff to next on-call (rajan): current state MONITORING, error rate 0.2%, mitigation in place (exp route removed, caches flushed), action items assigned. Logs and dashboards linked in INC-2025

rajan: thanks alex, I have all context. will monitor overnight and escalate if >0.5% sustained

sre_lead: good handoff. please post a short note in #eng-oncall at start of your watch

rajan: will do

product-emma: for org learnings: after postmortem let's do a 30m brown-bag demo of \"safe experiments\" and gating metrics

incident-bot: reminder scheduled: postmortem meeting INC-2025 on 2025-03-16T16:00Z

alex: closing notes: grateful for quick response. main prevention pattern = stricter experiment rollout + auto-rollback on KV miss spike

maya: note for runbook: include a 'safe mode' flag to prevent routing to heavy variants during high tail latencies

cs_jordan: customer comms drafted, sending in 10m

ops-taylor: closing monitoring loop; will leave sticky in the doc for next steps

sre_lead: big thanks team. we'll capture learnings in retro and schedule the brown-bag. Incident closed when postmortem published."
